Frogner — Oslo, Norway

Average day Average night

In detail

Frogner is one of Oslo's 15 official bydeler (city boroughs). Oslo kommune's own police-sourced Statistikkbanken data recorded 6,791 reported offences with their place of occurrence here in 2024, across a population of 60,727 residents — a rate of 11,183 offences per 100,000 residents, close to the citywide average. This rate is calculated against registered residents, not footfall, so a busy central or nightlife/shopping-heavy bydel can read higher without that meaning it is unusually risky to walk through, and a quiet residential bydel can show a low rate simply by having few offences relative to its population. This is Wandroz's official-data layer for Oslo — real Oslo kommune Statistikkbanken figures, not a qualitative or press-based judgment — and the source data is not split here by time of day, so both figures shown here are the same.

Frequently asked questions

Is Frogner safe?

Wandroz currently rates Frogner in Oslo, Norway as roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz during the day and roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz at night. This is a qualitative first-pass assessment based on general local knowledge and public reputation, not an official geolocated crime dataset — see the note on data limitations below before treating it as more precise than it is.

Is Frogner safe at night?

At night, Frogner is rated as roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Frogner a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Frogner's day rating (roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
